result: Prior research establishes TRIO as a neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) risk gene with two GEF domains (GEF1 activating Rac1/RhoG, GEF2 activating RhoA) that regulate neuronal development and synaptic function. Different TRIO variant types are associated with distinct NDDs, but the impact of heterozygous variants in vivo has not been explored.
evaluation: Claims C1-C25 are well-supported by extensive citations to prior literature establishing TRIO's role in NDDs, its biochemical functions, and clinical associations. The gap in knowledge (C25) provides clear rationale for the current study. These background claims appropriately contextualize the research.

result: Three NDD-associated Trio variants were generated in mice: K1431M (ASD-associated, impairs GEF1 activity), K1918X (SCZ-associated, leads to nonsense-mediated decay), and M2145T (BPD-associated, reduces GEF2 activity). Heterozygous mice for all three variants survived to adulthood. K1918X reduced Trio9 protein levels by ~50%, while K1431M and M2145T did not alter Trio isoform levels.
evaluation: Claims C26-C41 are well-supported by in vitro GEF assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B), Western blots (Figure 1C-D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-L), genotyping data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), and citations to prior work. The characterization of the mouse models is thorough and demonstrates successful generation of the intended variants with expected molecular consequences.

result: Trio variants differentially impact Rho GTPase activity in the brain. K1918X mice showed decreased Rac1 activity at P0 but not P42. Unexpectedly, K1431M mice exhibited increased Rac1 activity at both P0 (111%) and P42 (150%) despite the variant impairing GEF1 activity in vitro. M2145T mice showed decreased RhoA activity in P42 cortical synaptosomes (73% of WT) but not in whole brain lysates.
evaluation: Claims C42-C48 are supported by G-LISA assay data (Figure 1E-J). The unexpected increase in Rac1 activity in K1431M mice (C45, C47) is particularly notable and well-documented, representing a key finding that contradicts in vitro predictions. The compartment-specific effects in M2145T mice (C48) are appropriately identified. Statistical significance is reported with appropriate p-values.

result: Trio variant mice exhibit distinct behavioral phenotypes modeling NDD symptoms. K1431M and K1918X mice showed impaired motor coordination and learning on the rotarod. K1431M mice of both sexes and K1918X females showed social interaction deficits. K1918X mice of both sexes and M2145T females showed impaired novel object recognition. K1431M and K1918X males exhibited increased compulsive nestlet shredding.
evaluation: Claims C49-C54 are supported by comprehensive behavioral testing data (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). The behavioral battery is appropriate for assessing NDD-relevant phenotypes. Statistical analyses using two-way ANOVA with post-hoc tests are appropriate. The sex-specific differences are noted and appropriately reported. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=9-40 per group).

result: Trio variants differentially affect brain and head size. K1431M mice showed reduced head width and brain weight relative to body weight, driven by increased body weight. K1918X mice showed reduced brain weight-to-body weight ratio, reduced cortical thickness, and decreased layer 2/3 and layer 5 thickness. M2145T mice showed no significant changes. No changes in cortical cell density or neuron numbers were observed in any variant.
evaluation: Claims C55-C61 are supported by anatomical measurements (Figure 3A-J, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and immunostaining analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-N). The normalization to body weight is appropriate given the weight differences. The finding that K1918X brain size reduction is due to neuropil loss rather than cell number changes (C61) is well-supported. Statistical analyses are appropriate.

result: Trio variants cause modest but distinct changes in dendritic arbor morphology of M1 L5 pyramidal neurons. K1918X neurons showed reduced basal and apical dendritic arbor complexity and field size. K1431M neurons showed increased proximal basal arbor complexity. M2145T neurons showed decreased distal apical arbor complexity and field size. No changes in dendritic spine density were observed in any variant.
evaluation: Claims C62-C65 are supported by dendritic arbor reconstructions and Sholl analysis (Figure 3K-O, Figure 3—figure supplement 1-2). The use of Thy1-GFP mice for visualization is appropriate. The finding of no changes in spine density (C65) is notable given prior work with conditional knockouts. Statistical analyses using one-way and two-way ANOVA are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=15-22 neurons per group) are adequate.

result: Electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural synaptic changes in Trio variant mice. K1918X mice showed increased synapse density and slightly decreased PSD length. M2145T mice showed increased densities of docked and tethered vesicles at the active zone (readily releasable pool) and increased reserve pool vesicles. Presynaptic bouton and spine head areas were unchanged in all variants.
evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are supported by electron microscopy data (Figure 4). The measurements are appropriate and well-quantified. The interpretation that increased docked/tethered vesicles represent an enlarged RRP (C69) is consistent with established methods. The inference about larger SV pool size in M2145T (C70) is reasonable given the data. Sample sizes (5-18 fields per mouse, n=15-30 synapses) are adequate for EM analysis.

result: Trio variants differentially affect excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission. K1431M and K1918X mice showed increased AMPAR mEPSC amplitudes with no frequency changes, while M2145T showed increased AMPAR mEPSC frequency with unchanged amplitudes. NMDAR mEPSC frequencies were decreased in K1431M and increased in M2145T. K1431M and K1918X showed decreased NMDA/AMPA ratios. mIPSC frequencies were decreased in K1431M and M2145T, while K1918X showed increased mIPSC amplitude.
evaluation: Claims C71-C77 are supported by comprehensive electrophysiological recordings (Figure 5A-I). The recordings are technically sound with appropriate controls (TTX, receptor antagonists). Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=9-26 neurons from ≥5-8 mice per group) are adequate. The differential effects on AMPAR vs NMDAR and excitatory vs inhibitory transmission are well-documented and represent important findings.

result: Trio variants differentially affect long-term potentiation (LTP) in M1 L5 pyramidal neurons. WT mice showed robust LTP induction and potentiation. K1431M and K1918X mice showed deficient LTP induction and potentiation. M2145T mice showed increased LTP induction and prolonged potentiation compared to WT.
evaluation: Claims C78-C80 are supported by LTP recordings following theta-burst stimulation (Figure 5L-M). The protocol is appropriate and the results are clear. Statistical analysis using repeated measures two-way ANOVA is appropriate. Sample sizes (n=6-8 neurons from ≥4-5 mice per group) are adequate for LTP experiments. The bidirectional effects on LTP are striking and well-documented.

result: Trio variants differentially affect presynaptic glutamate release. K1431M mice showed enhanced paired-pulse facilitation at short ISIs, suggesting reduced probability of release (Pr). M2145T mice showed a complex PPR curve with reduced PPF at short ISIs and increased PPF at longer ISIs, indicating increased Pr and larger readily releasable pool (RRP). High-frequency stimulation confirmed decreased Pr in K1431M and increased Pr and RRP in M2145T. K1431M mice showed slower recovery rate after depletion.
evaluation: Claims C83-C88 are supported by paired-pulse ratio measurements (Figure 6A-B) and high-frequency stimulation analysis (Figure 6C-G). The use of the 'Decay' method to estimate Pr and RRP is appropriate and well-cited. The inferences about Pr from PPR data (C83, C85) are standard interpretations. Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=12-34 neurons from ≥5-9 mice per group) are adequate. These findings represent novel insights into Trio's presynaptic role.

result: Proteomic analysis of P21 cortex revealed distinct molecular signatures for each Trio variant. GSEA showed variant-specific pathway alterations, with synaptic vesicle pathway downregulation specific to K1431M. SynGO analysis restricted to brain-specific genes showed enrichment of differentially expressed proteins in synaptic processes for all variants. M2145T upregulated and K1431M downregulated proteins were enriched at the presynapse, while K1918X showed postsynaptic enrichment.
evaluation: Claims C89-C94 are supported by quantitative proteomics data (Figure 7A-C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). The proteomics approach is appropriate with adequate sample size (n=4 per genotype). GSEA and SynGO analyses are appropriate bioinformatics tools. The finding of presynaptic enrichment in K1431M and M2145T (C92) aligns well with the electrophysiology data. FDR correction is appropriately applied. The proteomics provides important molecular context for the functional findings.

result: Western blot analysis of P42 cortical synaptosomes and lysates revealed variant-specific changes in presynaptic proteins and Rho GEFs. M2145T synaptosomes showed increased Munc18-1, Syt3, and Syp levels. K1431M synaptosomes showed decreased Stx1a levels. Tiam1 levels were increased in both K1431M and M2145T cortical lysates. VAV2 levels were increased in M2145T lysates. Kalirin levels were unchanged in all variants.
evaluation: Claims C95-C99 are supported by Western blot data from synaptosomes (Figure 7D-H) and cortical lysates (Figure 7I-L). The protein targets are well-chosen and relevant to the observed functional phenotypes. The finding of increased Tiam1 in K1431M (C97) provides a potential mechanism for the unexpected increase in Rac1 activity. Statistical analyses using unpaired t-tests or one-way ANOVA are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=6-14 mice per group) are adequate.

result: Acute Rac1 inhibition with NSC23766 rescued glutamate release deficits in K1431M mice. NSC treatment shifted PPF downward in both WT and K1431M slices, suggesting increased Pr. NSC significantly increased Pr without affecting RRP size in both genotypes, rescuing the initial Pr deficit in K1431M. NSC increased the fractional recovery rate in both genotypes but did not fully rescue the slower recovery in K1431M. These results demonstrate that presynaptic Trio GEF1-dependent Rac1 signaling is crucial for maintaining synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment.
evaluation: Claims C101-C105 are supported by comprehensive rescue experiments using NSC23766 (Figure 8). The pharmacological approach is appropriate and the Rac1 inhibitor is well-characterized. The partial rescue of recovery rate (C104) is notable and suggests additional mechanisms beyond Rac1. Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=12-18 neurons from ≥5 mice per group) are adequate. This represents a key mechanistic finding linking elevated Rac1 activity to the presynaptic deficits in K1431M mice.

result: Heterozygosity for different NDD-associated Trio variants yields overlapping but distinct phenotypes in mice across behavioral, neuroanatomical, and synaptic domains. The variants differentially impact pre- and post-synaptic functions, with K1431M and M2145T showing prominent presynaptic deficits and K1918X showing more postsynaptic effects. These findings demonstrate that discrete TRIO variants cause both shared and distinct defects that may reflect variant-specific NDD clinical phenotypes.
evaluation: Claims C3-C6, C10, C107, C110, C150, C152 represent the overarching conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the comprehensive characterization across multiple experimental modalities (behavior, anatomy, electrophysiology, proteomics). The integration of findings across levels of analysis is appropriate. The conclusion that variants cause overlapping but distinct phenotypes is strongly supported by the data. The link to variant-specific NDD phenotypes is reasonable but somewhat speculative given the mouse model limitations.

result: The K1431M variant impairs TRIO GEF1 activity in vitro but paradoxically leads to increased Rac1 activity in postnatal K1431M mouse brains. This increase aligns with observed phenotypes and reveals why anticipated reductions in brain volume, dendrites, and AMPAR signaling were not observed. The increased Rac1 activity reflects homeostatic compensation occurring between birth and adult ages, potentially driven by upregulation of other Rac1 GEFs like Tiam1, while Kalirin does not compensate. Elevated Rac1 activity drives the reduction in synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment in K1431M mice.
evaluation: Claims C7-C8, C119-C124, C141 describe a key mechanistic finding of the study. The paradoxical increase in Rac1 activity despite impaired GEF1 function is well-documented by in vitro assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B), G-LISA measurements (Figure 1E, G, I), and Western blots showing increased Tiam1 (Figure 7I-L). The homeostatic compensation hypothesis (C122) is reasonable given the developmental time course. The link to presynaptic deficits (C141) is supported by NSC rescue experiments (Figure 8). This represents an important and unexpected finding.

result: Trio plays an essential role in presynaptic glutamate release and synaptic vesicle recycling. Trio localizes presynaptically and interacts with active zone proteins. Rac1 activity levels bidirectionally affect SV probability of release in excitatory synapses, negatively regulating synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment. Trio GEF1 and GEF2-mediated Rho GTPase signaling pathways play critical and distinct roles in regulating Pr, RRP size, and SV recycling.
evaluation: Claims C11, C81-C82, C100, C105, C109, C140, C149 describe the novel presynaptic role of Trio demonstrated in this study. These claims are supported by paired-pulse ratio data (Figure 6A-B), high-frequency stimulation analysis (Figure 6C-G), synaptic vesicle distribution measurements (Figure 4F-G), and NSC rescue experiments (Figure 8). The prior literature on Trio's presynaptic localization (C81) and Rac1's role in release (C82, C100, C140) is appropriately cited. This represents a major advance in understanding Trio function.

result: The phenotypes observed in Trio variant mice parallel clinical features in humans with TRIO mutations. K1431M and K1918X mice show reduced brain size consistent with microcephaly in patients with GEF1-deficient variants. K1918X mice show reduced cortical thickness similar to SCZ patients and NEX-Trio+/fl mice. Weight changes in K1431M and K1918X mice may relate to Rac1's role in insulin secretion. Dendritic alterations in K1918X mice are consistent with reports in SCZ patients.
evaluation: Claims C111-C118 appropriately contextualize the mouse findings relative to human clinical phenotypes. The parallels drawn are reasonable and well-supported by citations to clinical literature (C111-C113, C117) and prior mouse studies (C113). The speculation about weight changes relating to Rac1's role in insulin secretion (C114-C115) is reasonable but remains speculative. The comparison to NEX-Trio+/fl mice (C118) is appropriate and highlights the value of studying heterozygous variants.

result: The synaptic compartment is a key locus of Trio function, with spatiotemporally precise balance of Rac/Rho activity mediating cytoskeletal rearrangements. Altered Rho GTPase activation is an important mechanism affecting synaptic function in ASD and represents a convergent pathway and potential therapeutic target for NDDs. The findings support growing evidence linking synaptic dysfunction in NDD models to Rho GTPase signaling dysregulation.
evaluation: Claims C125-C129, C153 place the findings in broader context regarding Rho GTPase signaling in NDDs. The inference about the synaptic compartment being a key locus (C125) is supported by the synaptosome data. The claims about spatiotemporal balance (C126) and Rho GTPases as a convergent pathway (C128-C129, C153) are well-supported by citations to prior literature and the current findings. The suggestion of Rho GTPases as therapeutic targets (C129, C153) is reasonable but speculative.

result: The observed changes in AMPAR-mediated transmission and LTP in Trio variant mice can be explained by altered Rac1 activity and its effects on AMPAR trafficking and synaptic strength. Increased AMPAR in K1431M mice may reflect reduced silent synapses due to increased AMPAR incorporation driven by elevated Rac1. Developmental changes in Rac1 activity in K1918X mice may enhance AMPAR tone and affect LTP. The variants dysregulate excitatory and inhibitory transmission in different patterns, resulting in E/I imbalance.
evaluation: Claims C130-C138 provide mechanistic interpretations of the synaptic transmission and plasticity data. The interpretations are reasonable and well-supported by citations to prior work on Rac1's role in AMPAR trafficking (C130-C131, C136) and LTP (C135-C137). The inference about reduced silent synapses in K1431M (C132) is reasonable given the data. The developmental hypothesis for K1918X (C133) is plausible given the time course of Rac1 activity changes. The conclusion about E/I imbalance (C134) is well-supported by the mEPSC and mIPSC data.

result: The presynaptic effects of Trio variants can be explained by known roles of Trio, Rac1, and RhoA in regulating exocytosis and neurotransmitter release. Rac1 negatively regulates neurotransmitter release by increasing actin filament assembly at the active zone. In K1431M mice, opposing pre- and post-synaptic effects may mask expected changes in AMPAR mEPSC frequency. In M2145T mice, increased levels of Munc18, Syp, and Syt3 contribute to enhanced Pr and altered SV cycling, with altered Syt3 potentially explaining the unusual PPR.
evaluation: Claims C139, C143-C148 provide mechanistic interpretations of the presynaptic findings. The interpretations are reasonable and well-supported by citations to prior work on Trio/Rac1/RhoA in exocytosis (C139-C140, C143-C144). The hypothesis about opposing effects masking frequency changes in K1431M (C145) is plausible. The link between increased presynaptic proteins and enhanced Pr in M2145T (C147) is reasonable. The speculation about Syt3 explaining the unusual PPR (C148) is plausible but remains speculative. The acknowledgment that RhoA's specific role is unclear (C146) is appropriate.

result: Large-scale genetic studies show significant overlap in NDD risk genes converging on synaptic proteins. The current findings extend prior work on Trio's postsynaptic roles and demonstrate for the first time that the K1431M lesion in TRIO GEF1 leads to presynaptic deficits due to Rac1 dysregulation, which can be rescued by pharmacological normalization.
evaluation: Claims C106, C108, C151 summarize key contextual and concluding points. The claim about overlap in NDD risk genes (C106) is well-supported by citations to large-scale genetic studies. The claim about extending prior work on postsynaptic roles (C108) is appropriate. The claim about demonstrating presynaptic deficits and pharmacological rescue (C151) is well-supported by the NSC experiments (Figure 8) and represents a major finding of the study.
